novatienda.s.cliente-01-login.title: Sign in
novatienda.s.cliente-01-login.desc: Customer sign-in with email and password, or in one tap with Google. It offers a remember-me option and a visible password-recovery link. After several failed attempts the platform asks for an anti-bot check. A link takes new visitors straight to registration.
novatienda.s.cliente-02-registro.title: Sign up
novatienda.s.cliente-02-registro.desc: Sign-up form with an optional personal or company ID, name, surnames, email and phone. Every field is validated as the user types (the phone, for instance, follows the 8888-8888 format). The password must meet a minimum length and strength. New users must accept the terms and privacy policy, and that acceptance is recorded.
novatienda.s.cliente-03-recuperar-contra: Customers enter their email and receive instructions to choose a new password. The emailed link is single-use and expires, and the reply is the same whether or not the account exists, so it never reveals who is registered. Changing the password signs out any previous sessions.
novatienda.s.cliente-04-inicio.title: Home
novatienda.s.cliente-04-inicio.desc: A landing page that works like a shop window: a clear message, a featured product with its price in colones and an add-to-cart button, and two more products beside it. Below it, the stores with their opening hours and a best-sellers carousel. Visitors see what is sold, what it costs and where to pick it up on one screen.
novatienda.s.cliente-04-inicio.alt: Store home page with a featured product.
novatienda.s.cliente-05-tienda.title: Store
novatienda.s.cliente-05-tienda.desc: A catalog organized for quick discovery: a category bar with arrows and dropdown subcategories, a name search and round category shortcuts. Carousels for promotions, best sellers and new arrivals, each with its own “See all” button. Every card shows a favorites heart, the price and a one-tap add to cart.
novatienda.s.cliente-05-tienda.alt: Store catalog with categories and carousels.
novatienda.s.cliente-06-tienda-todos-los: The full catalog with combinable filters by category, brand and more, sorted by newest. It shows how many products match and clears the filters in one click. Pagination lets visitors choose how many products to see per page. On phones, the filters open in a separate panel.
novatienda.s.cliente-07-contacto.title: Contact
novatienda.s.cliente-07-contacto.desc: A direct line to the business: customers write their name, email and message, and the platform opens WhatsApp with everything pre-filled, so there is no inbox to monitor. It includes social links and one card per store with address, hours, phone and “How to get there”. A frequently-asked-questions section closes the page.
novatienda.s.cliente-07-contacto.alt: Contact page with form and store locations.
novatienda.s.cliente-08-mi-cuenta.title: My account
novatienda.s.cliente-08-mi-cuenta.desc: The customer's personal area, split into sections: my details, delivery address, orders, reviews and security. They can update their information with per-field validation, follow the status of their orders. Under Security they turn on two-step verification with an authenticator app.
novatienda.s.cliente-08-mi-cuenta.alt: My account area with the customer's personal details.
novatienda.s.cliente-09-favoritos.title: Favorites
novatienda.s.cliente-09-favoritos.desc: The list of products the customer marked with a heart, ready to resume shopping. Each card shows the image, name and price, and lets the customer remove the product or open its page. It is a shortcut for shoppers who compare several options before deciding.
novatienda.s.cliente-10-carrito.title: Cart
novatienda.s.cliente-10-carrito.desc: Customers review what they are about to buy: image, color, editable quantity, price and weight of each product. A summary computes the subtotal, total weight and an estimated shipping cost based on weight, with the choice of home delivery or free in-store pickup. It closes with the total and the proceed-to-payment button.
novatienda.s.cliente-10-carrito.alt: Shopping cart with summary and delivery method.
novatienda.s.cliente-11-producto.title: Product
novatienda.s.cliente-11-producto.desc: Everything a buyer needs to decide: a gallery of photos and videos, price in colones, warranty, color variants and available units. A panel shows the stock level at each store, so buyers know where to pick up. It adds buy-now, add to cart or favorites, ask on WhatsApp, the technical sheet and reviews.
novatienda.s.cliente-11-producto.alt: Product page with gallery, price and per-store availability.
novatienda.s.cliente-12-checkout.title: Checkout
novatienda.s.cliente-12-checkout.desc: Order summary and confirmation on a single page: contact details, delivery method, an address with cascading province, canton and district, and loyalty points that can be redeemed as a discount. For store pickup, customers choose a store that has the whole order. Payment is completed on the secure Onvopay gateway; the shop never sees or stores card data.
novatienda.s.cliente-12-checkout.alt: Checkout screen with delivery details and order summary.
novatienda.s.negocio-01-dashboard.title: Dashboard
novatienda.s.negocio-01-dashboard.desc: The business at a glance: sales, orders, average ticket, new customers, profit, margin, best-selling product and low-stock products, each compared with the previous period. Sales and profit charts over time and a monthly goal. It filters by date range and by store, and exports to PDF.
novatienda.s.negocio-01-dashboard.alt: Dashboard with KPIs and sales charts.
novatienda.s.negocio-02-pedidos.title: Orders
novatienda.s.negocio-02-pedidos.desc: Every order in a table with search and filters by status, shipping method and store. From the detail view, the team changes the status (processing, shipped, delivered), records the postal tracking number and proof of delivery, and can reassign the order to another store. Every change is audited and notifies the customer.
novatienda.s.negocio-03-productos.title: Products
novatienda.s.negocio-03-productos.desc: The complete catalog with image, price, cost, stock, weight and status, plus filters by category, status, brand and date. When creating or editing a product, the team uploads photos, up to three videos, color and size variants, warranty and each store's stock. It includes bulk selection and access to the tax data for e-invoicing.
novatienda.s.negocio-04-inventario.title: Inventory
novatienda.s.negocio-04-inventario.desc: The stock of every variant in every store, one column per store plus the total. Quantities below the minimum are highlighted with an alert, and a filter shows only what needs restocking. From here, units are transferred between stores, and each transfer is kept in a history showing who made it.
novatienda.s.negocio-05-tiendas.title: Stores
novatienda.s.negocio-05-tiendas.desc: Store management: location, phone, opening hours, units in inventory, open orders and each store's monthly sales goal. Stores can be created, edited, activated and deactivated; the platform blocks deactivating one that has orders in progress. This data automatically feeds the footer, the contact page and the checkout.
novatienda.s.negocio-06-reportes.title: Reports
novatienda.s.negocio-06-reportes.desc: Reports on sales and revenue, profit, inventory, customers, promotions and reviews. Each one offers sub-reports (by product, category, brand, area or customer), a date-range and store filter, and Excel and PDF export. The figures come from the same data as the dashboard, so they always match.
novatienda.s.negocio-06-reportes.alt: Sales report with filters and export.
novatienda.s.negocio-07-facturacion.desc: The electronic tax documents of each sale, as required by Costa Rica's tax authority: receipts, invoices and credit notes with their status, sequence number, total and store. A summary counts those in progress, accepted, with problems or discarded. A failed submission can be retried and the files downloaded. Invoicing is issued automatically once the payment is confirmed.
novatienda.s.negocio-08-configuracion.de: The business details the team can change without technical help: social networks, contact phone and email, the company's legal data and the monthly sales goal. Every field is validated (the WhatsApp number, for instance), and whatever is saved is reflected on the public site, in the footer and in the legal texts.
novatienda.s.negocio-09-clientes.title: Customers
novatienda.s.negocio-09-clientes.desc: The list of registered customers and their purchase activity: number of orders, total spent and loyalty points earned. It is searchable by name or email and sortable, for example from highest to lowest spend, to spot the best customers. Each row opens a detail view with the customer's history.
novatienda.s.negocio-10-usuarios.title: Users
novatienda.s.negocio-10-usuarios.desc: Staff accounts with their role, the stores they can see, their two-step verification status and whether they are active. Each person sees and edits only what belongs to their own stores. The platform stops anyone from changing accounts with more privileges than their own or granting themselves more permissions than they hold.
novatienda.s.negocio-11-roles.title: Roles & permissions
novatienda.s.negocio-11-roles.desc: The panel's roles, with how many people hold each one. For every role you define, module by module, what it can do: view, create, edit or delete. A store manager can run their orders and inventory without reaching the settings. System roles are protected, and a role that still has users cannot be deleted by mistake.
novatienda.s.negocio-12-auditoria.title: Audit log
novatienda.s.negocio-12-auditoria.desc: The log of everything that happens: who did what, in which module, on which store and when. It records changes to the catalog, orders, stock, users and payments, plus sign-ins. It filters by module, action, user, store and dates, and “View detail” shows exactly which value changed. The log cannot be edited from the panel.
novatienda.s.negocio-13-notificaciones.d: The panel's bell alerts the team to whatever needs attention: new orders, low-stock products and reassigned orders. Each alert reaches only the right people, based on their store and permissions. They can be marked as read one by one or all at once, and the counter shows how many are still pending.

art.sw.b01: When a business decides to go digital, the same question almost always comes up: do I start with a website, an online store or a mobile app? All three options work, but they solve different problems. Choosing wrong means spending time and money on something your customers will not use.
art.sw.b02: This guide helps you decide based on what you sell, who you sell to and how you want to be found.
art.sw.b03: First, define what you want to achieve
art.sw.b04: Before thinking about technology, answer three questions:
art.sw.b05.1: What do you want your visitor to do? Call you, message you on WhatsApp, buy, or come back every week?
art.sw.b05.2: What do you sell? A service that is quoted case by case, or products that can be bought on the spot?
art.sw.b05.3: How many times a month does a typical customer come back? Once a year, or many times a month.
art.sw.b06: Your answers almost always point to one of the three options.
art.sw.b08: A website is your business card on the internet. It explains what you do, shows your work and gives people a clear way to contact you.
art.sw.b09: It is the best option if:
art.sw.b10.1: You offer services that are quoted (consulting, construction, technology, health, education).
art.sw.b10.2: You want to be found on Google when someone searches for what you do.
art.sw.b10.3: You need to build trust before people contact you.
art.sw.b11: What it must have: clear information about what you offer, your location and service area, a visible button to message you on WhatsApp or call you, and fast loading on mobile. Most visits come from a phone, so if the site looks bad on a small screen, you lose customers.
art.sw.b12: Its limit: an informational site does not take payments or manage orders. If you want to sell online, you need to take one more step.
art.sw.b13: Online store: selling 24 hours a day
art.sw.b14: An online store is a website that also lets people choose products, pay and track their order. The value for you is that it sells even while you sleep, and that it keeps inventory, orders and invoicing in one place. To see what one looks like inside, check out NovaTienda, an example of an online store with an admin panel that we built.
art.sw.b15: It is the best option if:
art.sw.b16.1: You sell products that can be described with photos and a price.
art.sw.b16.2: You want to sell beyond your area or receive orders outside business hours.
art.sw.b16.3: Today you manage orders through messages and payments, stock or deliveries get tangled.
art.sw.b17: What to check before setting one up:
art.sw.b18.1: Payment methods your customers use. In Costa Rica it pays to use a reliable payment gateway and to plan how you will collect and reconcile.
art.sw.b18.2: Shipping and in-store pickup. Define how orders are delivered and what it costs.
art.sw.b18.3: Inventory and invoicing. If you sell little, a simple system is enough; if you sell a lot, you need stock and electronic invoices to update on their own.
art.sw.b18.4: Who manages it. A store without a control panel, where every change means calling a technician, becomes a problem.
art.sw.b19: Mobile app: for customers who come back often
art.sw.b20: Your own mobile app makes sense when your customer interacts with you often: orders food, books appointments, checks their account, collects points or receives notifications.
art.sw.b21: It is the best option if:
art.sw.b22.1: Your customers come back many times a month and you want to make their life easier.
art.sw.b22.2: You need notifications, a user account or features that an ordinary website does not offer well.
art.sw.b22.3: You have a service where convenience is part of what you sell.
art.sw.b24.1: It is the option that requires the most work and maintenance.
art.sw.b24.2: If your customers only buy from you now and then, they will most likely not download it.
art.sw.b24.3: There is a middle ground: a website or online store designed for mobile that can be installed on the phone like an app (known as a PWA). For many businesses it offers much of the convenience of an app without the cost of building and publishing a separate one.
art.sw.b25: How to choose: a quick guide
art.sw.t.r1c1: You offer services and want to be found and contacted
art.sw.t.r2c1: You sell products and want to charge and manage orders online
art.sw.t.r3c1: Your customers interact with you very often
art.sw.t.r3c2: Mobile app, or a store installable as a PWA
art.sw.t.r4c1: You are just starting and are not sure
art.sw.t.r4c2: Start with a clear website and grow from there
art.sw.b28: The most frequent mistake is starting with the biggest option. Many businesses ask for an app when what they need is a fast-loading website and a well-placed WhatsApp button. Others set up a store without thinking about how they will deliver orders.
art.sw.b29: The best strategy is almost always to start with the essentials, measure what people use and grow step by step. A well-built site today can become a store tomorrow, without starting from scratch.
art.sw.cta.h: Not sure which one to choose?
art.sw.cta.p: At Vanguard Solutions we build websites, online stores and mobile apps for businesses and companies of all sizes in Costa Rica. Tell us what you sell and how you work, and we will help you choose the option that truly fits, without selling you more than you need. See all our services.

art.pn.title: Google Business Profile: how to get found on Google Maps | Vanguard Solutions
art.pn.desc: What the Google Business Profile is, how to create and verify it, and how to keep it up to date so your business shows up when people search nearby.
art.pn.b01: When someone searches for “optician near me” or “clinic in Cartago”, the first thing they see is not your website: it is a card with each business's name, phone number, opening hours and reviews. That card is called the Google Business Profile, it is free, and it is the most important thing for being found nearby. This guide explains how to create it, verify it and keep it up to date.
art.pn.b02: What it is and why it matters
art.pn.b03: The Business Profile is your card in Google Search and Google Maps. It shows your business name, phone number, opening hours, services, photos and reviews. For local searches it is the most important piece, and it also feeds the information panel that appears on the right of the results. Creating it costs nothing, but it requires a verification that can take several days.
art.pn.b04: Before you start: do you serve customers at a location?
art.pn.b05: If your customers come to a location, Google shows the address. If you serve people at their place or online, you can hide the address and set a service area. Decide this before you create the profile.
art.pn.b06: Create the profile step by step
art.pn.b07.1: Use your business's real name. Do not add keywords to it: Google penalizes that.
art.pn.b07.2: Choose the main category carefully and add related secondary categories.
art.pn.b07.3: Enter your address or your service area.
art.pn.b07.4: Add your phone number, your website and, if you like, the WhatsApp chat link.
art.pn.b07.5: Write a description of up to 750 characters, without links, prices or promotions.
art.pn.b07.6: Fill in your opening hours, services and photos. Upload your square logo (720×720 px) and a cover photo.
art.pn.b09: Google needs to confirm that the business exists. Depending on what it offers in your case, verification can be by phone call, text message, email or video. It can take several days: do it as soon as you can and wait for the approval before considering the profile finished.
art.pn.b11.3: Keep your opening hours up to date.
art.pn.b11.4: Ask your satisfied customers for reviews, without offering anything in return.
art.pn.b12: The golden rule: the same name, address and phone number everywhere
art.pn.b13: Write them exactly the same on your website, your profile and any directory. This consistency is called NAP, for name, address and phone number. Small changes, such as “Avenida 2” in one place and “Av. 2” in another, make the data not match.
art.pn.b15: Nobody can guarantee that your profile will show up first. What is in your hands is having it verified, complete, with the same data everywhere and with real, answered reviews.
art.pn.cta.h: If you want us to do it for you
art.pn.cta.p: In our website plans we set up Search Console and the Google Business Profile (and Bing in Standard and Professional). We need a Google account for your business and your involvement to verify it. See the plans or message us on WhatsApp.

art.sd.title: Don't fall for “7-day” websites: what a good site really needs | Vanguard Solutions
art.sd.desc: A site built in a week can look good and be of no use. What a professional site needs and what to ask before you hire.
art.sd.h1: Don't fall for “7-day” websites: what a good site really needs
art.sd.b01: Have you seen ads like “Your website ready in 24 hours” or “Your website ready in 7 days or less, and very cheap”? There are more and more offers like these, and it is easy to see why: artificial intelligence tools can generate a page that looks good in minutes. The problem is that looking good is not the same as working for your business.
art.sd.b02: A website is not a template
art.sd.b03: A site that serves a business starts by understanding that business: who it sells to, what it wants visitors to do, what sets it apart and how people will find it. Then come the design, the content, the programming, testing on different devices, security, launch and maintenance. Skipping those steps is what makes it possible to deliver “in 7 days”, and it is also what leaves an empty shell: a page that looks nice on the outside, with no strategy or foundations inside.
art.sd.b04: AI speeds things up, but it does not replace engineering
art.sd.b05: AI tools are useful in the hands of someone who knows how to program: they save time on repetitive tasks. In the hands of someone who does not, they produce code that nobody reviews. A 2025 Veracode report tested more than 100 language models on 80 programming tasks and found that, in 45% of the cases, the generated code included OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities. Models are getting better at writing code that works, but not at writing it securely. It is a study of controlled tasks, not of published websites, but it shows the risk of trusting code that nobody reviews.
art.sd.b06: Why it matters in Costa Rica
art.sd.b07: Your website is the face of your business and it handles your customers' data. According to the OIJ's 2025 Annual Report, reports of computer fraud went from 7,260 in 2024 to 10,059 in 2025, and those of website impersonation from 173 to 205. The UNA's Cybersecurity Laboratory (Labcibe) points out that computer fraud grew 1,446% between 2019 and 2025. Those figures are about crimes, not about developers, but they show that a site without HTTPS, without updates and without anyone looking after it is an unnecessary risk for your brand and your customers.
art.sd.b09.1: They promise a complete site in 1 to 7 days for a very low price.
art.sd.b09.2: They ask you nothing about your business, your customers or what you want to achieve.
art.sd.b09.3: They do not show you a prototype before programming.
art.sd.b09.4: They do not tell you in whose name the domain, the hosting and the code are held.
art.sd.b09.5: They ask for full payment up front and nothing is in writing.
art.sd.b09.6: They do not explain what happens if something fails after delivery.
art.sd.b09.7: They cannot tell you who builds the site or what training and experience that person has.
art.sd.b10: What a professional site should include
art.sd.b11.1: Understanding your business and defining what the site must achieve.
art.sd.b11.2: A prototype and adjustments before the final version.
art.sd.b11.3: Design that looks good on phones and computers.
art.sd.b11.4: Basic security: HTTPS, a form with spam protection and a privacy policy.
art.sd.b11.7: A warranty and maintenance after delivery.
art.sd.b13: We are software engineers with a university education, and the person who answers you is the one who builds your project. One of our sites takes between 2 and 6 weeks depending on the plan, because it includes a prototype and adjustments, and it is paid in three installments. What you hire is put in writing: what is included, what is not, in whose name the domain and hosting are held, and a 12-month warranty against bugs and critical security failures.
